title: The Student at the Front

sentences.en: Every Friday afternoon, the last class in Room 302 looks a little strange.
sentences.zh: 每周五下午，302 教室的最后一节课看起来有点奇怪。

sentences.en: The teacher sits at the back, and a student stands at the front holding a piece of chalk.
sentences.zh: 老师坐在后面，一名学生站在前面，手里拿着一支粉笔。

sentences.en: For twenty minutes, that student explains a lesson that the class studied earlier in the week.
sentences.zh: 有二十分钟，这名学生讲解全班这周早些时候学过的一课。

sentences.en: This practice began two years ago, when a teacher noticed something that surprised her.
sentences.zh: 这个做法始于两年前，当时一位老师注意到了一件让她吃惊的事。

sentences.en: Students who could answer questions in class often failed to explain the same idea to a friend.
sentences.zh: 那些能在课堂上回答问题的学生，常常无法把同样的内容讲给朋友听。

sentences.en: They recognized the words but could not rebuild the logic behind them.
sentences.zh: 他们认得那些词，却无法重建词背后的逻辑。

sentences.en: Researchers call this the teaching effect, and it has been tested many times.
sentences.zh: 研究者称之为教学效应，这一效应已被多次检验。

sentences.en: In one experiment, students who prepared a lesson for others remembered far more than those who studied for a test.
sentences.zh: 在一项实验中，为他人准备课程的学生，记住的内容远多于为考试而学习的学生。

sentences.en: The reason is simple: teaching forces you to find the gaps in your own understanding.
sentences.zh: 原因很简单：教学迫使你发现自己理解中的空白。

sentences.en: When you try to explain a rule, you quickly discover which part you never really learned.
sentences.zh: 当你试着解释一条规则时，你会很快发现哪一部分自己从未真正学会。

sentences.en: The method is not perfect, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这个方法并不完美。

sentences.en: It takes time, and shy students may feel nervous at first.
sentences.zh: 它需要时间，害羞的学生一开始可能会紧张。

sentences.en: But most of them say that standing at the front taught them more than listening ever did.
sentences.zh: 但他们中的大多数人说，站在前面讲课教给他们的，比一直听讲要多。

keyVocab.note: 此处不是练习，而是指一种固定做法
强调见过、认得，不等于理解
gaps in understanding 指理解上的漏洞
feel nervous at first 一开始会紧张

grammar.en: For twenty minutes, that student explains a lesson that the class studied earlier in the week.
grammar.main: that student explains a lesson
grammar.subject: that student
grammar.modifiers: For twenty minutes 是时间状语；that the class studied earlier in the week 是定语从句修饰 a lesson，关系词 that 在从句中作 studied 的宾语
grammar.logic: 主句用一般现在时描述每周固定的安排，定语从句补充说明这堂课是本周早些时候学过的内容
grammar.zh: 有二十分钟，这名学生讲解全班这周早些时候学过的一课。

grammar.en: This practice began two years ago, when a teacher noticed something that surprised her.
grammar.main: This practice began two years ago
grammar.subject: This practice
grammar.object: 无（began 在此为不及物动词）
grammar.modifiers: two years ago 是时间状语；when 引导非限制性定语从句修饰 two years ago；从句里 that surprised her 又是定语从句修饰 something
grammar.logic: 用 when 从句交代做法产生的时间和起因，把上一段的观察与这一段的由来连起来
grammar.zh: 这个做法始于两年前，当时一位老师注意到了一件让她吃惊的事。

grammar.en: When you try to explain a rule, you quickly discover which part you never really learned.
grammar.main: you quickly discover which part you never really learned
grammar.subject: you
grammar.object: which part you never really learned（宾语从句）
grammar.modifiers: When you try to explain a rule 是时间状语从句；quickly 是方式状语
grammar.logic: 时间状语从句设定情境，主句用宾语从句说明发现的具体内容
grammar.zh: 当你试着解释一条规则时，你会很快发现哪一部分自己从未真正学会。

quiz.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A class where students take turns teaching a lesson
Why Friday classes are shorter than other classes
How to prepare for a written test
The design of a new school building
quiz.evidence: The teacher sits at the back, and a student stands at the front holding a piece of chalk.
quiz.explain: 全文围绕周五由学生上台讲课这一做法展开，先描述场景，再说明原理，最后指出局限，主旨是这种课堂形式。
whyWrong: 文中没有比较周五与其他日子的课时长短。
为考试而学习只是实验中的对照组，并非介绍备考方法。
全文没有涉及教学楼的设计。

quiz.question: What problem did the teacher notice?
options: Students forgot everything during the weekend.
Students could repeat an idea but not explain it.
Students refused to answer questions in class.
Students preferred writing to speaking.
quiz.evidence: They recognized the words but could not rebuild the logic behind them.
quiz.explain: 原文说学生认得词却重建不了背后的逻辑，即能复述、不能讲解，与选项中的 repeat 与 not explain 对应。
whyWrong: 文中没有提到周末遗忘的问题。
学生是能回答课堂提问的，并不是拒绝回答。
文中没有比较写作与口语的偏好。

quiz.question: The word 'gaps' in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ___?
options: long silences
holes in a wall
parts you have not understood
marks left by chalk
quiz.evidence: The reason is simple: teaching forces you to find the gaps in your own understanding.
quiz.explain: gaps 与 understanding 搭配，指理解中缺失的部分，下一句的 which part you never really learned 正是解释。
whyWrong: 文中讨论的是理解，不是沉默的时间长短。
这里是比喻用法，不是指墙上的洞。
粉笔痕迹与理解缺失无关。

quiz.question: What is the author's attitude towards the Friday class?
options: Completely opposed to it
Uncertain about its value
Supportive but aware of its limits
Interested only in the time it saves
quiz.evidence: The method is not perfect, of course.
quiz.explain: 作者承认方法不完美、费时间、会让害羞的学生紧张，但结尾说它教得更多，态度是支持而清醒。
whyWrong: 作者列举了不足，但整体是肯定的，并非完全反对。
作者态度明确，没有表现出犹豫。
文中没有提到这种方法节省时间，反而说它费时间。

title: The Cost of Being Guided

sentences.en: Ten years ago, most drivers in a new city had to stop and ask for directions.
sentences.zh: 十年前，在陌生的城市里，大多数司机都得停下车问路。

sentences.en: Today they simply follow a voice that tells them when to turn.
sentences.zh: 如今他们只需跟着一个声音走，那个声音会告诉他们什么时候转弯。

sentences.en: Navigation apps have made travel easier, but they have also changed the way our brains work.
sentences.zh: 导航应用让出行更方便，但也改变了我们大脑的工作方式。

sentences.en: A study at a university in London asked volunteers to travel through an imaginary neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 伦敦一所大学的研究让志愿者在一个想象中的街区里行走。

sentences.en: Those who followed step-by-step instructions found their way back easily, but remembered very little of the streets.
sentences.zh: 那些按一步步指示行走的人很容易找回原路，却几乎记不住街道的样子。

sentences.en: Those who explored without help made mistakes, yet they built a mental map that stayed with them for weeks.
sentences.zh: 那些独自摸索的人会走错路，却在大脑中建起了一张能保留数周的地图。

sentences.en: The difference matters because a mental map does more than guide us home.
sentences.zh: 这种差别很重要，因为大脑中的地图不只是把我们带回家。

sentences.en: It helps us notice when a route is blocked and decide what to do next.
sentences.zh: 它帮我们察觉某条路线被阻断，并决定下一步怎么办。

sentences.en: When we always follow instructions, we practise following rather than thinking.
sentences.zh: 当我们总是照着指示走时，我们练习的是服从，而不是思考。

sentences.en: In other words, the app learns the city while we forget it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，应用学会了这座城市，而我们把它忘了。

sentences.en: This does not mean we should throw away our phones.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们该把手机扔掉。

sentences.en: A simple habit may be enough: check the map before you leave, then put the phone away for the first few streets.
sentences.zh: 一个简单的习惯也许就够了：出发前看一眼地图，然后在前几条街上把手机收起来。

sentences.en: You will probably get lost once or twice, and that is exactly when your brain starts to build the map.
sentences.zh: 你可能会迷路一两次，而正是在那时，你的大脑才开始绘制地图。

keyVocab.note: 英式拼写，美式为 practice（动词）

grammar.en: Those who followed step-by-step instructions found their way back easily, but remembered very little of the streets.
grammar.main: Those found their way back easily, but remembered very little of the streets
grammar.subject: Those（后接 who 定语从句）
grammar.object: their way back / very little of the streets
grammar.modifiers: who followed step-by-step instructions 是定语从句修饰 Those；easily 是方式状语
grammar.logic: but 连接两个并列谓语，构成对比：找路轻松，但对街道几乎没有记忆
grammar.zh: 那些按一步步指示行走的人很容易找回原路，却几乎记不住街道的样子。

grammar.en: Those who explored without help made mistakes, yet they built a mental map that stayed with them for weeks.
grammar.main: Those made mistakes, yet they built a mental map
grammar.subject: Those / they
grammar.modifiers: who explored without help 修饰 Those；that stayed with them for weeks 是定语从句修饰 a mental map
grammar.logic: yet 表转折，与上一句形成对照：会犯错的人反而记住了城市
grammar.zh: 那些独自摸索的人会走错路，却在大脑中建起了一张能保留数周的地图。

grammar.en: When we always follow instructions, we practise following rather than thinking.
grammar.main: we practise following rather than thinking
grammar.subject: we
grammar.object: following rather than thinking（动名词短语作宾语）
grammar.modifiers: When we always follow instructions 是时间状语从句；rather than 引出被否定的对比项
grammar.logic: 从句给出条件，主句点明后果：总是照做，练的其实是服从
grammar.zh: 当我们总是照着指示走时，我们练习的是服从，而不是思考。

quiz.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How navigation apps affect the maps in our minds
Why paper maps are more accurate than apps
How to choose the best navigation app
The history of road building in London
quiz.evidence: Navigation apps have made travel easier, but they have also changed the way our brains work.
quiz.explain: 文章先摆出导航带来的便利，再用实验说明它对脑中地图的影响，最后给出折中建议，主题是导航与空间记忆的关系。
whyWrong: 文中没有比较纸质地图与应用的准确度。
全文没有提供挑选应用的方法。
伦敦只是实验地点，不是文章主题。

quiz.question: What happened to the volunteers who explored without help?
options: They never found their way back.
They remembered the streets for a long time.
They refused to join the study.
They drew a map on paper.
quiz.evidence: Those who explored without help made mistakes, yet they built a mental map that stayed with them for weeks.
quiz.explain: 原文说他们虽然会走错，却在脑中建起了能保留数周的地图，即长时间记得街道。
whyWrong: 他们只是走错路，最终是能找回方向的。
他们是自愿参加实验的志愿者，没有拒绝。
文中说的是脑中的地图，不是画在纸上的。

quiz.question: The word 'blocked' in paragraph 3 probably means ___?
options: closed off
made wider
newly painted
carefully measured
quiz.evidence: It helps us notice when a route is blocked and decide what to do next.
quiz.explain: 路线被 blocked 之后才需要决定下一步怎么走，可见意思是走不通、被封闭。
whyWrong: made wider 是变宽，与需要改道的语境相反。
newly painted 指新刷的漆，与路线能否通行无关。
carefully measured 指仔细测量，不能解释为何要另想办法。

quiz.question: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
options: People should stop using navigation apps completely.
Getting lost can be part of learning a city.
Phones are useless when you travel.
Maps should be printed before every trip.
quiz.evidence: You will probably get lost once or twice, and that is exactly when your brain starts to build the map.
quiz.explain: 作者说迷路一两次正是大脑开始绘图的时候，说明走错路本身有学习价值。
whyWrong: 作者明确说不必扔掉手机，只是建议偶尔收起来。
作者承认应用让出行更方便，并没有否定手机。
文中建议出发前查看地图，没有要求打印。

title: Why the Small Bookshop Still Stands

sentences.en: When a large online seller opened a warehouse outside the town, everyone expected the small bookshop on Bridge Street to close within a year.
sentences.zh: 当一家大型网络卖家在镇外建起仓库时，所有人都以为桥街那家小书店一年之内就会关门。

sentences.en: Five years later, it is still there, and its Saturday reading club has a waiting list.
sentences.zh: 五年过去，它还在那里，周六读书会甚至要排队等名额。

sentences.en: Its owner, a quiet woman named Chen, says the secret is not cheaper books.
sentences.zh: 店主是一位安静的女性，姓陈，她说秘诀不是更便宜的书。

sentences.en: Large sellers win on price because they buy in huge amounts and deliver quickly.
sentences.zh: 大型卖家在价格上占优势，因为它们大批量进货，而且送货很快。

sentences.en: A small shop cannot match that, so Chen stopped trying.
sentences.zh: 小店比不了这一点，于是陈不再去比。

sentences.en: Instead, she turned the shop into a place where people come to talk about what they read.
sentences.zh: 她转而把书店变成了一个人们来谈论所读之书的地方。

sentences.en: Every Thursday she invites a local teacher to lead a discussion for an hour.
sentences.zh: 每周四她请一位本地老师带领一小时的讨论。

sentences.en: Customers who arrive early can borrow a chair and a cup of tea.
sentences.zh: 早到的顾客可以借一把椅子和一杯茶。

sentences.en: Some of them buy nothing that evening, yet they return the following week with friends.
sentences.zh: 有些人那晚什么也没买，但下周会带着朋友再来。

sentences.en: Those friends often become the customers who pay full price without complaining.
sentences.zh: 这些朋友往往成了不抱怨、按全价付钱的顾客。

sentences.en: Business experts describe this as selling an experience rather than a product.
sentences.zh: 商业专家把这称为卖体验，而不是卖产品。

sentences.en: It works only when the experience is real, because customers can feel the difference immediately.
sentences.zh: 只有体验是真实的，这招才管用，因为顾客立刻就能感觉到差别。

sentences.en: For Chen, the lesson is simple: a shop that people want to keep will usually find a way to survive.
sentences.zh: 对陈来说，道理很简单：一家人们愿意留住的书店，通常总能找到活下去的办法。

keyVocab.note: 大型电商常靠仓库压低成本
商业语境中指企业活下来

grammar.en: When a large online seller opened a warehouse outside the town, everyone expected the small bookshop on Bridge Street to close within a year.
grammar.main: everyone expected the small bookshop to close within a year
grammar.subject: everyone
grammar.object: the small bookshop ... to close（宾语 + 不定式构成的复合宾语）
grammar.modifiers: When 引导时间状语从句；on Bridge Street 是后置定语修饰 bookshop；within a year 是时间状语
grammar.logic: 从句交代背景，主句用 expect sb to do 表达当时普遍的预期，为后文的转折做铺垫
grammar.zh: 当一家大型网络卖家在镇外建起仓库时，所有人都以为桥街那家小书店一年之内就会关门。

grammar.en: Instead, she turned the shop into a place where people come to talk about what they read.
grammar.main: she turned the shop into a place
grammar.subject: she
grammar.modifiers: where people come to talk about what they read 是定语从句修饰 a place；其中 what they read 是宾语从句作 about 的宾语
grammar.logic: Instead 承接上文放弃比价的做法，where 从句说明这个场所的具体功能
grammar.zh: 她转而把书店变成了一个人们来谈论所读之书的地方。

grammar.en: It works only when the experience is real, because customers can feel the difference immediately.
grammar.main: It works
grammar.subject: It
grammar.modifiers: only 限定条件；when the experience is real 是时间状语从句；because 从句说明原因
grammar.logic: when 从句给出成立条件，because 从句解释为什么必须真实，两句构成条件与原因的双重限制
grammar.zh: 只有体验是真实的，这招才管用，因为顾客立刻就能感觉到差别。

quiz.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a small bookshop survives by selling an experience
Why online sellers are losing customers
How to open a reading club in a town
The history of Bridge Street
quiz.evidence: Five years later, it is still there, and its Saturday reading club has a waiting list.
quiz.explain: 文章从书店没有倒闭写起，分析它放弃比价、改卖体验的做法，主旨是小店的生存策略。
whyWrong: 文中说大型卖家在价格上占优势，并未说它们流失顾客。
读书会只是书店的具体做法之一，不是全文主题。
桥街只是地点，文章没有讲它的历史。

quiz.question: What do some customers do on Thursday evenings?
options: They buy several books at a discount.
They stay without buying and return with friends.
They complain about the price.
They lead the discussion themselves.
quiz.evidence: Some of them buy nothing that evening, yet they return the following week with friends.
quiz.explain: 原文说有些人当晚什么都不买，下周却带朋友回来，正是选项所描述的行为。
whyWrong: 文中没有提到打折，反而强调有人按全价付款。
不抱怨、付全价的是后来成为顾客的朋友，不是周四的听众。
主持讨论的是受邀的本地老师。

quiz.question: The word 'match' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to ___?
options: be equal to
light a fire
find a pair
compete in a game
quiz.evidence: A small shop cannot match that, so Chen stopped trying.
quiz.explain: 前一句讲大型卖家的价格与送货优势，小店无法 match，即无法与之相当。
whyWrong: light a fire 是点火，与价格竞争无关。
find a pair 指配成一对，不符合此处比较的语境。
compete in a game 指参加比赛，文中说的是经营条件。

quiz.question: Why can large sellers offer lower prices?
options: They sell better books.
They buy in large amounts and deliver fast.
They receive money from the town.
They have no workers.
quiz.evidence: Large sellers win on price because they buy in huge amounts and deliver quickly.
quiz.explain: 原文直接用 because 说明原因：大批量进货、送货快，成本因此更低。
whyWrong: 文中没有评价书的质量高低。
文中没有提到任何来自镇上的补贴。
送货快说明它们有完整的物流和人力，并非没有员工。

title: Exercise in Small Pieces

sentences.en: Many people believe that exercise only counts if it lasts at least thirty minutes.
sentences.zh: 很多人相信，一次运动至少要持续三十分钟才算数。

sentences.en: This idea comes from old fitness advice, and it has made millions of people give up before they start.
sentences.zh: 这个观念来自过去的健身建议，它让无数人还没开始就放弃了。

sentences.en: Recent research suggests that short bursts of movement, spread through the day, can be just as useful.
sentences.zh: 近期研究表明，把短时间的活动分散到一天中，效果可能同样好。

sentences.en: In one study, office workers were asked to climb three floors of stairs four times a day.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，办公室职员被要求每天爬四次三层楼梯。

sentences.en: After twelve weeks, their blood pressure and resting heart rate had improved noticeably.
sentences.zh: 十二周后，他们的血压和静息心率都有明显改善。

sentences.en: None of them changed their diet, and none of them visited a gym.
sentences.zh: 他们中没有一个人改变饮食，也没有一个人去过健身房。

sentences.en: The reason is that the body does not ask how long a movement lasts.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，身体并不问你的一次动作持续多久。

sentences.en: It responds to how often the muscles are used and how hard they work.
sentences.zh: 它回应的是肌肉被使用的频率，以及用力有多大。

sentences.en: Climbing stairs, carrying shopping, or walking fast to catch a bus all count.
sentences.zh: 爬楼梯、提着购物袋，或者快走去赶公交，都算。

sentences.en: What matters is that the effort happens regularly, not that it happens in one long block.
sentences.zh: 关键在于这种用力经常发生，而不是集中在一大段时间里。

sentences.en: There is one caution, however.
sentences.zh: 不过，有一点需要注意。

sentences.en: Short bursts cannot replace training for a marathon, and they do not build strength on their own.
sentences.zh: 短时活动无法替代马拉松训练，也不能单独练出力量。

sentences.en: But for people who sit for most of the day, a few minutes of movement every hour may be the easiest change they will ever make.
sentences.zh: 但对一天中大部分时间都坐着的人来说，每小时动几分钟，也许是最容易做出的改变。

keyVocab.note: short bursts of movement 短时活动
此处用过去分词 spread 表被动
此处指需要提醒的一点

grammar.en: Recent research suggests that short bursts of movement, spread through the day, can be just as useful.
grammar.main: Recent research suggests that short bursts can be just as useful
grammar.subject: Recent research
grammar.modifiers: 宾语从句的主干是 short bursts of movement can be useful；spread through the day 是过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 bursts
grammar.logic: suggests 后的宾语从句承载全文论点，插入的过去分词短语补充说明活动的分布方式
grammar.zh: 近期研究表明，把短时间的活动分散到一天中，效果可能同样好。

grammar.en: In one study, office workers were asked to climb three floors of stairs four times a day.
grammar.main: office workers were asked to climb three floors of stairs
grammar.subject: office workers
grammar.object: to climb three floors of stairs（不定式作主语补足语）
grammar.modifiers: In one study 是状语；four times a day 是频率状语
grammar.logic: 被动语态把受试者放在句首，重点落在他们被要求做什么，而不强调是谁提出的要求
grammar.zh: 在一项研究中，办公室职员被要求每天爬四次三层楼梯。

grammar.en: What matters is that the effort happens regularly, not that it happens in one long block.
grammar.main: What matters is that ...
grammar.subject: What matters（主语从句）
grammar.object: that the effort happens regularly（表语从句）
grammar.modifiers: not that it happens in one long block 是与前一个表语从句并列的否定项，形成对比
grammar.logic: 主语从句加两个表语从句，构成重要的是甲、而不是乙的判断句式
grammar.zh: 关键在于这种用力经常发生，而不是集中在一大段时间里。

quiz.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Short bursts of movement can be as useful as long workouts.
Everyone should run a marathon once a year.
Gyms are the only place to build strength.
Office workers should stop using stairs.
quiz.evidence: Recent research suggests that short bursts of movement, spread through the day, can be just as useful.
quiz.explain: 全文围绕短时活动同样有效这一观点展开，用实验和研究解释原因，最后补充局限。
whyWrong: 文中说短时活动不能替代马拉松训练，并非鼓励人人跑马拉松。
实验中没有人去健身房，文章也没有说健身房是唯一选择。
爬楼梯恰恰是文中推荐的短时活动。

quiz.question: What happened to the office workers in the study?
options: Their diet changed completely.
Their blood pressure and heart rate improved.
They joined a gym nearby.
They stopped climbing stairs.
quiz.evidence: After twelve weeks, their blood pressure and resting heart rate had improved noticeably.
quiz.explain: 原文明确说十二周后血压和静息心率明显改善，与选项对应。
whyWrong: 原文说没有人改变饮食。
原文说没有人去过健身房。
他们正是被要求每天爬楼梯的。

quiz.question: The word 'bursts' in paragraph 1 probably means ___?
options: short periods
loud noises
long journeys
heavy meals
quiz.evidence: Recent research suggests that short bursts of movement, spread through the day, can be just as useful.
quiz.explain: bursts 由 short 修饰，又与 spread through the day 搭配，指分散在全天的短时段活动。
whyWrong: loud noises 是响声，与运动无关。
long journeys 指长途旅行，与 short 矛盾。
heavy meals 指油腻的一餐，与 movement 搭配不上。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about short bursts of exercise?
options: They are enough for marathon training.
They are helpful but have limits.
They only work for young people.
They replace the need for any other activity.
quiz.evidence: Short bursts cannot replace training for a marathon, and they do not build strength on their own.
quiz.explain: 文章肯定短时活动的价值，同时指出它不能替代专项训练、也无法单独增力，说明有效但有边界。
whyWrong: 原文明确说不能替代马拉松训练。
文中没有提到年龄差异。
原文说它不能单独练出力量，可见不能取代一切活动。

title: Museums Without Glass Cases

sentences.en: In most museums, the most important objects sit behind glass, and visitors are told not to touch them.
sentences.zh: 在大多数博物馆里，最重要的物件都摆在玻璃后面，参观者被告知不要触摸。

sentences.en: A new kind of museum is reversing that rule.
sentences.zh: 一种新型博物馆正在颠覆这条规矩。

sentences.en: At these places, touching is not a mistake but the whole point.
sentences.zh: 在这些地方，触摸不是错误，而是全部意义所在。

sentences.en: One example is a small museum in the north of the country that displays copies of ancient tools.
sentences.zh: 一个例子是该国北部的一家小博物馆，它展出古代工具的复制品。

sentences.en: Visitors can hold a stone knife, weigh a clay pot, or try to start a fire with a wooden stick.
sentences.zh: 参观者可以握一握石刀，掂一掂陶罐，或者试着用木棍取火。

sentences.en: The real objects remain in a locked room upstairs, safe from damage.
sentences.zh: 真正的物件被锁在楼上的一间屋子里，以免受损。

sentences.en: The museum's director explains that glass protects objects but also creates distance.
sentences.zh: 馆长解释说，玻璃保护了物件，却也制造了距离。

sentences.en: A child who sees a tool through a window learns its name; a child who holds it learns what it was for.
sentences.zh: 隔着窗看工具的孩子学到的是名称；把工具握在手里的孩子学到的是它的用途。

sentences.en: This matters because understanding the past requires imagination, and imagination needs something to work with.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为理解过去需要想象力，而想象力需要有东西可依托。

sentences.en: A smooth handle or a heavy pot gives the mind a starting point.
sentences.zh: 一个光滑的把手或一只沉重的罐子，给了头脑一个起点。

sentences.en: Critics warn that such museums may turn history into entertainment.
sentences.zh: 批评者警告说，这类博物馆可能把历史变成娱乐。

sentences.en: The director accepts the risk but argues that a visitor who remembers the weight of a pot will read about it later.
sentences.zh: 馆长接受这一风险，但认为记住罐子重量的参观者，之后会去读相关的书。

sentences.en: Curiosity, she says, is a better teacher than a warning sign.
sentences.zh: 她说，好奇心比警告牌是更好的老师。

keyVocab.note: reverse a rule 把一条规矩反过来
safe from damage 免受损坏

grammar.en: A child who sees a tool through a window learns its name; a child who holds it learns what it was for.
grammar.main: A child learns its name; a child learns what it was for
grammar.subject: A child / a child
grammar.object: its name / what it was for（宾语从句）
grammar.modifiers: who sees a tool through a window 与 who holds it 都是定语从句，分别修饰两个 a child
grammar.logic: 分号连接两个结构对称的分句，用看与摸的对照说明体验的价值
grammar.zh: 隔着窗看工具的孩子学到的是名称；把工具握在手里的孩子学到的是它的用途。

grammar.en: This matters because understanding the past requires imagination, and imagination needs something to work with.
grammar.main: This matters
grammar.subject: This
grammar.modifiers: because 引导原因状语从句；从句内部 understanding the past 是动名词短语作主语，and 连接两个并列分句
grammar.logic: because 从句给出理由，and 把需要想象力与想象力需要依托两层意思串起来
grammar.zh: 这很重要，因为理解过去需要想象力，而想象力需要有东西可依托。

grammar.en: The director accepts the risk but argues that a visitor who remembers the weight of a pot will read about it later.
grammar.main: The director accepts the risk but argues that ...
grammar.subject: The director
grammar.object: the risk / that 引导的宾语从句
grammar.modifiers: that a visitor ... will read about it later 是宾语从句；其中 who remembers the weight of a pot 是定语从句修饰 a visitor
grammar.logic: but 表示先让步再转折：承认风险，仍坚持自己的判断
grammar.zh: 馆长接受这一风险，但认为记住罐子重量的参观者，之后会去读相关的书。

quiz.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A museum that lets visitors touch copies of old objects
Why glass cases are expensive to build
How to start a fire with a wooden stick
The rules children must follow in museums
quiz.evidence: At these places, touching is not a mistake but the whole point.
quiz.explain: 文章介绍一类允许触摸复制品的博物馆，说明其理由，也提到争议，主题是这种新的展陈方式。
whyWrong: 文中没有讨论玻璃柜的造价。
取火只是参观者可以尝试的活动之一，不是主题。
文章恰恰在讲打破不许触摸的旧规矩。

quiz.question: Where are the real objects kept?
options: In the main hall
In a locked room upstairs
In a local school
Outside in the garden
quiz.evidence: The real objects remain in a locked room upstairs, safe from damage.
quiz.explain: 原文直接说明真品锁在楼上的房间里，以免损坏，展厅里供触摸的是复制品。
whyWrong: 主展厅里摆放的是供触摸的复制品。
文中没有提到学校参与存放。
文中没有提到把真品放在室外。

quiz.question: The word 'reversing' in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ___?
options: turning the other way
writing down again
repairing carefully
explaining in detail
quiz.evidence: A new kind of museum is reversing that rule.
quiz.explain: 上句说不许触摸，下句说触摸才是重点，可见 reversing 是把规矩反过来。
whyWrong: writing down again 指重新抄写，与规矩的改变无关。
repairing carefully 指修缮，文中没有提到修理。
explaining in detail 指详细解释，不能解释规矩被打破。

quiz.question: What is the author's attitude towards such museums?
options: Strongly critical
Generally favourable
Completely uninterested
Worried only about money
quiz.evidence: A child who sees a tool through a window learns its name; a child who holds it learns what it was for.
quiz.explain: 作者用对称的对比句强调触摸更能带来理解，末段虽引出批评，但以馆长的回应收尾，整体态度是肯定的。
whyWrong: 批评意见只是转述，作者本人并未持强烈否定态度。
作者花了大量篇幅解释其价值，并非漠不关心。
文中没有讨论经费问题。

title: The River That Came Back

sentences.en: Thirty years ago, the river that runs through the industrial district was the color of weak tea.
sentences.zh: 三十年前，流经工业区的那条河颜色像淡茶。

sentences.en: Factory waste poured into it, and residents kept their windows closed on hot days.
sentences.zh: 工厂废料被倒进去，居民在热天也关着窗。

sentences.en: Fish had disappeared, and children were warned never to go near the water.
sentences.zh: 鱼消失了，孩子们被警告绝不要靠近河水。

sentences.en: The change began in 2005, when the city government closed the pipes that carried untreated water into the river.
sentences.zh: 变化始于 2005 年，市政府封堵了把未处理的水排入河中的管道。

sentences.en: Engineers then built small wetlands along the banks, where plants could filter the water slowly.
sentences.zh: 工程师随后在两岸建起小型湿地，植物可以在那里慢慢过滤水质。

sentences.en: At first, few people believed it would work.
sentences.zh: 起初，很少有人相信这能行。

sentences.en: The river was too polluted, they said, and the cost was too high.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这条河污染太严重，代价也太高。

sentences.en: Ten years later, the results were visible to anyone who walked past.
sentences.zh: 十年后，任何路过的人都能看到结果。

sentences.en: Water birds returned first, followed by fish that had not been seen since the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 水鸟先回来了，接着是从 20 世纪 80 年代以来就没见过的鱼。

sentences.en: Today the banks are a park, and on summer evenings the paths are full of families.
sentences.zh: 如今两岸是一座公园，夏天的傍晚，小路上满是家庭。

sentences.en: Property prices near the river have risen, which has pushed some old residents further away.
sentences.zh: 河边的房价上涨了，这也把一些老居民挤到了更远的地方。

sentences.en: The lesson is not that pollution can always be undone cheaply.
sentences.zh: 这个教训并不是说污染总能被廉价地修复。

sentences.en: It is that a river, like most living systems, can recover if the source of harm is removed and time is allowed for healing.
sentences.zh: 而是说，一条河和大多数生命系统一样，只要切断伤害的来源并给予时间，就能恢复。

keyVocab.note: untreated water 未经处理的水
植物与湿地可以自然过滤水质
主语可以是人，也可以是生态系统

grammar.en: Thirty years ago, the river that runs through the industrial district was the color of weak tea.
grammar.main: the river was the color of weak tea
grammar.subject: the river
grammar.object: the color of weak tea（表语）
grammar.modifiers: that runs through the industrial district 是定语从句修饰 the river；Thirty years ago 是时间状语
grammar.logic: 定语从句插在主语和谓语之间，先限定是哪一条河，再给出它当时的状态
grammar.zh: 三十年前，流经工业区的那条河颜色像淡茶。

grammar.en: Engineers then built small wetlands along the banks, where plants could filter the water slowly.
grammar.main: Engineers built small wetlands
grammar.subject: Engineers
grammar.modifiers: along the banks 是地点状语；where plants could filter the water slowly 是非限制性定语从句修饰 wetlands
grammar.logic: where 从句补充说明湿地的功能，解释上句所说的治理办法为什么有效
grammar.zh: 工程师随后在两岸建起小型湿地，植物可以在那里慢慢过滤水质。

grammar.en: Property prices near the river have risen, which has pushed some old residents further away.
grammar.main: Property prices have risen
grammar.subject: Property prices
grammar.modifiers: near the river 是后置定语修饰 prices；which 引导非限制性定语从句，指代前面整句的内容
grammar.logic: which 从句引出前面事实带来的意外后果，为末段的辩证结论做铺垫
grammar.zh: 河边的房价上涨了，这也把一些老居民挤到了更远的地方。

quiz.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How a polluted river was brought back to life
Why factories should be closed permanently
How to build a park along a river
The history of the industrial district
quiz.evidence: It is that a river, like most living systems, can recover if the source of harm is removed and time is allowed for healing.
quiz.explain: 文章按时间顺序写一条河从污染到恢复的过程，结尾点明主旨：切断污染源并给予时间，河流可以恢复。
whyWrong: 文中只提到工厂停止排污，没有主张永久关闭所有工厂。
建公园是恢复后的结果，不是文章要讲的方法。
工业区只是背景，文章重点在河流的变化。

quiz.question: What did the city government do in 2005?
options: It built new factories.
It closed the pipes carrying untreated water.
It moved residents away from the river.
It planted trees along the banks.
quiz.evidence: The change began in 2005, when the city government closed the pipes that carried untreated water into the river.
quiz.explain: 原文说市政府封堵了输送未处理污水的管道，这是治理的起点。
whyWrong: 文中没有新建工厂，反而在减少排污。
居民是被房价推走的，不是政府迁走的。
工程师建的是湿地，文中没有说种树。

quiz.question: The word 'filter' in paragraph 2 probably means ___?
options: clean by passing through something
carry away quickly
freeze in cold weather
measure with a tool
quiz.evidence: Engineers then built small wetlands along the banks, where plants could filter the water slowly.
quiz.explain: 植物让水慢慢流过，从而去除杂质，这就是 filter 的意思，slowly 也提示了净化的过程。
whyWrong: carry away quickly 是快速冲走，与 slowly 和净化的目的不符。
freeze 指结冰，与水质改善无关。
measure 指测量，不能解释水为何变清。

quiz.question: What does the rise in property prices suggest?
options: The cleanup brought benefits and also problems.
The river is still heavily polluted.
No one wants to live near the river.
The government has stopped the project.
quiz.evidence: Property prices near the river have risen, which has pushed some old residents further away.
quiz.explain: 房价上涨说明环境变好、地价上升，但老居民被迫搬远，可见治理同时带来了新的社会问题。
whyWrong: 房价上涨恰恰说明环境改善，不是仍在污染。
房价上涨说明人们愿意住在河边。
文中没有任何项目停止的信息。

title: Why a Tomato Costs More in Winter
titleZh: 冬天的番茄为什么更贵

sentences.en: In summer, tomatoes fill the market and prices fall so low that sellers almost give them away.
sentences.zh: 夏天，番茄堆满市场，价格低到卖家几乎是白送。

sentences.en: In January, the same tomato may cost three times as much.
sentences.zh: 到了一月，同样的番茄可能要贵上三倍。

sentences.en: The difference is not greed; it is a simple lesson in supply and demand.
sentences.zh: 差别不在贪婪，而在一条关于供求的简单道理。

sentences.en: When local fields stop producing, shops must buy from regions hundreds of kilometers away.
sentences.zh: 当本地田地停止产出，商店只能从数百公里外的地区进货。

sentences.en: Transport adds fuel, labor and cooling costs to every box.
sentences.zh: 运输会给每一箱加上燃料、人工和冷藏成本。

sentences.en: Some tomatoes travel by ship and truck for more than a week, and a few are damaged on the way.
sentences.zh: 有些番茄要坐船和卡车走上一个多星期，路上还会损坏一些。

sentences.en: Demand, meanwhile, does not fall in winter.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，需求在冬天并没有下降。

sentences.en: People still want salad, and restaurants still put tomato in their dishes.
sentences.zh: 人们仍然想吃沙拉，餐馆仍然往菜里放番茄。

sentences.en: When supply drops and demand stays the same, the price rises.
sentences.zh: 当供给下降而需求不变，价格就会上涨。

sentences.en: Economists call this elasticity, and it explains why some goods become expensive while others stay cheap.
sentences.zh: 经济学家称之为弹性，它解释了为什么有些商品变贵，而另一些仍然便宜。

sentences.en: There are ways to soften the effect.
sentences.zh: 有办法可以缓和这种影响。

sentences.en: Greenhouses can grow vegetables near the city, and better storage can keep fruit fresh for longer.
sentences.zh: 温室可以在城市附近种菜，更好的储存能让果蔬保鲜更久。

sentences.en: Both cost money, so the winter tomato will never be as cheap as the summer one.
sentences.zh: 两者都要花钱，所以冬天的番茄永远不会像夏天那么便宜。

sentences.en: Understanding why may at least stop us from putting the blame on the shopkeeper.
sentences.zh: 明白其中原因，至少能让我们不再把责任推到店主身上。

keyVocab.note: 经济学中指价格对供求变化的敏感程度
put the blame on sb 把责任推到某人身上

grammar.en: In summer, tomatoes fill the market and prices fall so low that sellers almost give them away.
grammar.main: tomatoes fill the market and prices fall
grammar.subject: tomatoes / prices
grammar.modifiers: so low that sellers almost give them away 是 so...that 结果状语从句，修饰 low；In summer 是时间状语
grammar.logic: and 连接两个并列分句，第二句用 so...that 引出结果：价格低到几乎白送
grammar.zh: 夏天，番茄堆满市场，价格低到卖家几乎是白送。

grammar.en: When local fields stop producing, shops must buy from regions hundreds of kilometers away.
grammar.main: shops must buy from regions
grammar.subject: shops
grammar.object: 无（from regions 是地点状语）
grammar.modifiers: When local fields stop producing 是时间状语从句；hundreds of kilometers away 是名词短语作后置定语修饰 regions
grammar.logic: 从句交代季节条件，主句说明由此产生的采购行为，两者构成因果
grammar.zh: 当本地田地停止产出，商店只能从数百公里外的地区进货。

grammar.en: Economists call this elasticity, and it explains why some goods become expensive while others stay cheap.
grammar.main: Economists call this elasticity, and it explains why ...
grammar.subject: Economists / it
grammar.object: this elasticity / why 引导的宾语从句
grammar.modifiers: why 从句中 while others stay cheap 是对比状语从句，与 some goods become expensive 形成对照
grammar.logic: and 承接前句，用 why 从句把经济学术语落到具体现象上
grammar.zh: 经济学家称之为弹性，它解释了为什么有些商品变贵，而另一些仍然便宜。

quiz.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why tomato prices change with the seasons
How to grow tomatoes in a greenhouse
Why shopkeepers are often dishonest
The best way to store fresh fruit
quiz.evidence: The difference is not greed; it is a simple lesson in supply and demand.
quiz.explain: 文章以番茄为例，用供给、运输和需求解释季节性价差，主题是价格随季节变动的原因。
whyWrong: 温室只是末段提到的一种缓解办法，不是主题。
文章明确说差别不在贪婪，也没有指责店主。
储存只是缓解手段之一，全文重点在价格。

quiz.question: Why do winter tomatoes cost more?
options: They taste better than summer ones.
They must be brought from far away.
Fewer people want to buy them.
Shops refuse to sell them cheaply.
quiz.evidence: When local fields stop producing, shops must buy from regions hundreds of kilometers away.
quiz.explain: 本地田地在冬天停产，商店只能远距离采购，运输和损耗推高了成本。
whyWrong: 文中没有比较冬天与夏天番茄的味道。
文中说需求在冬天并没有下降。
价格由供求与成本决定，不是店主故意不卖便宜。

quiz.question: The word 'soften' in paragraph 4 probably means ___?
options: make less severe
make completely disappear
make louder
make more expensive
quiz.evidence: There are ways to soften the effect.
quiz.explain: 后文举温室和储存两个办法，都是让涨价的影响变小，故 soften 是减弱、缓和。
whyWrong: make completely disappear 指彻底消失，而末句说冬天番茄永远不会和夏天一样便宜。
make louder 指声音变大，与价格影响无关。
make more expensive 与缓和影响的意思相反。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about greenhouse vegetables?
options: They are always cheaper than field vegetables.
They cost more but reduce the seasonal gap.
They are impossible to grow near cities.
They damage the soil in winter.
quiz.evidence: Both cost money, so the winter tomato will never be as cheap as the summer one.
quiz.explain: 温室能在城市附近种菜，缓解冬季缺货，但成本高，所以只能缩小价差而不能消除。
whyWrong: 末句说冬天番茄永远不会像夏天那么便宜。
文中明确说温室可以在城市附近种菜。
文中没有提到温室破坏土壤。

title: The Sunday Reset

sentences.en: For a long time, my Sunday evenings were the worst part of my week.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，我的周日晚上是一周中最糟的部分。

sentences.en: I would lie on the sofa, think about the work waiting for me, and feel the weekend slipping away.
sentences.zh: 我会躺在沙发上，想着等着我的工作，感觉周末正在溜走。

sentences.en: Then a friend suggested something so simple that I almost ignored it.
sentences.zh: 后来一个朋友提了个简单到我差点忽略的建议。

sentences.en: She told me to use thirty minutes on Sunday afternoon to prepare for Monday, not to worry about it.
sentences.zh: 她让我在周日下午用三十分钟为周一做准备，而不是为它发愁。

sentences.en: I chose three small tasks: washing clothes, cooking rice for two days, and writing a short list of what I had to finish.
sentences.zh: 我选了三件小事：洗衣服、煮好两天的米饭、写一张要完成事项的短清单。

sentences.en: None of these tasks was difficult, and together they took less than half an hour.
sentences.zh: 这些事都不难，加起来不到半小时。

sentences.en: The effect was surprising.
sentences.zh: 效果令人意外。

sentences.en: Because the boring jobs were already done, Monday morning no longer felt heavy.
sentences.zh: 因为那些乏味的活儿已经做完，周一早晨不再显得沉重。

sentences.en: Because the list was short, I could see exactly where to begin.
sentences.zh: 因为清单很短，我一眼就能看到从哪里开始。

sentences.en: The worry did not disappear, but it stopped growing in the dark.
sentences.zh: 担忧没有消失，但它不再在黑暗里长大。

sentences.en: Psychologists explain that unfinished tasks take up space in the mind.
sentences.zh: 心理学家解释说，未完成的任务会占据心里的空间。

sentences.en: Writing them down tells the brain that they are recorded, so it can let go for a while.
sentences.zh: 把它们写下来，等于告诉大脑它们已被记录，于是它可以暂时放下。

sentences.en: My Sunday reset is not a cure for a busy life, but it has given me back one quiet evening each week.
sentences.zh: 我的周日重启不是忙碌生活的解药，但它每周还给我一个安静的晚上。

keyVocab.note: almost ignored it 差点没当回事
affect 是动词，effect 是名词

grammar.en: Then a friend suggested something so simple that I almost ignored it.
grammar.main: a friend suggested something
grammar.subject: a friend
grammar.modifiers: so simple that I almost ignored it 中，so simple 作后置定语修饰 something，that 从句是结果状语从句
grammar.logic: so...that 结构把简单和差点忽略连成因果关系，为下文的转折蓄势
grammar.zh: 后来一个朋友提了个简单到我差点忽略的建议。

grammar.en: Because the boring jobs were already done, Monday morning no longer felt heavy.
grammar.main: Monday morning no longer felt heavy
grammar.subject: Monday morning
grammar.modifiers: Because the boring jobs were already done 是原因状语从句，从句用被动语态；no longer 是否定意义的频度状语
grammar.logic: 原因在前、结果在后，直接点明周日准备与周一心情之间的因果
grammar.zh: 因为那些乏味的活儿已经做完，周一早晨不再显得沉重。

grammar.en: Writing them down tells the brain that they are recorded, so it can let go for a while.
grammar.main: Writing them down tells the brain that ...
grammar.subject: Writing them down（动名词短语作主语）
grammar.object: the brain（间接宾语）+ that 从句（直接宾语）
grammar.modifiers: so it can let go for a while 是 so 引导的结果状语从句
grammar.logic: 动名词作主语提出做法，that 从句说明告知的内容，so 从句给出结果
grammar.zh: 把它们写下来，等于告诉大脑它们已被记录，于是它可以暂时放下。

quiz.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A small Sunday routine that made Mondays easier
How to cook rice for a whole week
Why weekends are shorter than weekdays
The best way to clean a flat
quiz.evidence: My Sunday reset is not a cure for a busy life, but it has given me back one quiet evening each week.
quiz.explain: 文章讲作者周日花半小时做几件小事，从而让周一不再沉重，主旨是这个小习惯带来的改变。
whyWrong: 煮饭只是三件小事之一，不是主题。
文章没有比较周末与工作日的长短。
打扫只是其中一项，全文重点在心理上的变化。

quiz.question: What did the writer do on Sunday afternoon?
options: She met a friend for coffee.
She finished three small tasks.
She wrote a long report.
She cleaned the whole flat.
quiz.evidence: I chose three small tasks: washing clothes, cooking rice for two days, and writing a short list of what I had to finish.
quiz.explain: 原文列出三件小事：洗衣服、煮饭、写清单，与选项中的 three small tasks 对应。
whyWrong: 朋友只是提建议的人，文中没有写周日见面喝咖啡。
她写的是短清单，不是长报告。
文中只说洗衣服，没有说打扫整个房子。

quiz.question: The word 'reset' in the title probably means ___?
options: a fresh start before the week begins
a broken machine
a long holiday
a difficult exam
quiz.evidence: She told me to use thirty minutes on Sunday afternoon to prepare for Monday, not to worry about it.
quiz.explain: 标题中的 reset 指在周日前花半小时整理状态，为新一周重新开始做准备。
whyWrong: 文中讲的是人的状态调整，不是机器故障。
只有半小时，谈不上长假。
文中没有提到考试。

quiz.question: Why does writing tasks down help?
options: It makes the tasks shorter.
It tells the mind the tasks are recorded.
It removes all the work.
It helps the writer sleep longer.
quiz.evidence: Writing them down tells the brain that they are recorded, so it can let go for a while.
quiz.explain: 原文说写下来等于告诉大脑事情已被记录，大脑因此可以暂时放下，焦虑就不再累积。
whyWrong: 写下来只是记录，不会让事情本身变少或变短。
任务依然存在，只是不再占据心思。
文中谈的是心理负担，没有提到睡眠时长。

title: A Better Way to Practise

sentences.en: When Nina began learning English, she copied a list of twenty words every evening.
sentences.zh: 妮娜开始学英语时，每晚抄写一张包含二十个单词的词表。

sentences.en: The pages looked neat, but she often forgot the words when she needed them in conversation.
sentences.zh: 笔记看起来很整齐，但她在对话中需要用这些词时常常想不起来。

sentences.en: She decided to change the way she practised rather than simply spend more time at her desk.
sentences.zh: 她决定改变练习方式，而不是一味延长坐在书桌前的时间。

sentences.en: First, she chose five useful words from a short article that she could mostly understand.
sentences.zh: 首先，她从一篇基本能读懂的短文中挑出五个实用词。

sentences.en: For each word, she wrote a sentence about her own day and read it aloud.
sentences.zh: 她用每个词写一句与自己当天生活有关的话，并大声读出来。

sentences.en: The next morning, she covered the notes and tried to remember the sentences before checking them.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，她盖住笔记，先尝试回忆这些句子，再核对。

sentences.en: Some words were still difficult, so she reviewed them again after a few days.
sentences.zh: 有些词仍然很难，她便过几天再次复习。

sentences.en: She also kept reading, which gave familiar words new situations and made their meanings clearer.
sentences.zh: 她也坚持阅读，让熟悉的词出现在新情境中，使词义更加清晰。

sentences.en: Her progress was gradual, but now her notebook supported real use instead of becoming a collection of copied pages.
sentences.zh: 她的进步是逐渐发生的，但现在笔记本帮助她实际运用语言，而不再只是一叠抄写页。

sentences.en: When a word returned in another article, she could connect the two examples and notice a difference.
sentences.zh: 当一个词在另一篇文章中再次出现时，她能联系两条例句，留意其中的差别。

grammar.en: She decided to change the way she practised rather than simply spend more time at her desk.
grammar.zh: 她决定改变练习方式，而不是一味延长坐在书桌前的时间。
grammar.main: She decided to change the way
grammar.subject: She
grammar.object: to change the way she practised
grammar.modifiers: she practised 修饰 way；rather than 对比两种选择。
grammar.logic: 改变方法与单纯增加时长形成对照。

grammar.en: She also kept reading, which gave familiar words new situations and made their meanings clearer.
grammar.zh: 她也坚持阅读，让熟悉的词出现在新情境中，使词义更加清晰。
grammar.main: She also kept reading
grammar.subject: She
grammar.modifiers: which 引导非限制性定语从句，概括继续阅读的效果。
grammar.logic: which 从句中的 gave 和 made 并列，说明阅读的两方面帮助。

quiz.question: What change improves Nina's learning?
options: Copying longer lists more neatly
Avoiding all difficult words
Reading only her own notes
Using and recalling words in meaningful sentences
quiz.evidence: The next morning, she covered the notes and tried to remember the sentences before checking them.
quiz.explain: 她加入个人例句、主动回忆和持续阅读，使学习服务于实际使用。
whyWrong: 笔记整齐却不会用正是原来的问题。
难词并未被放弃，而是再次复习。
她仍然阅读文章以获得新语境。

quiz.question: What does Nina do before checking her notes?
options: She asks a friend for the answers
She stops reading for a week
She tries to remember her sentences
She copies twenty new words
quiz.evidence: The next morning, she covered the notes and tried to remember the sentences before checking them.
quiz.explain: 她先盖住笔记回忆，随后核对。
whyWrong: 文中没有朋友提供答案。
文章强调她保持阅读。
二十词抄写是此前采用的方法。

quiz.question: What does the writer suggest about progress?
options: It requires forgetting old words
It may be slow while still being useful
It must appear after one evening
It depends on a neat notebook alone
quiz.evidence: Her progress was gradual, but now her notebook supported real use instead of becoming a collection of copied pages.
quiz.explain: gradual 表明进步并非立刻发生，但已经提升真实使用能力。
whyWrong: 复习的目标是记住而非遗忘旧词。
末句明确说进步是渐进的。
整洁笔记本并不足以让她会运用。

title: Before You Share the Story

sentences.en: An exciting headline appeared in a student group one afternoon, claiming that the college library would close for a whole year.
sentences.zh: 一天下午，学生群里出现一条引人注意的标题，声称学校图书馆将关闭整整一年。

sentences.en: Several people immediately shared it with friends, and others complained without opening the link.
sentences.zh: 几个人立刻转发给朋友，另一些人还没打开链接就开始抱怨。

sentences.en: Jia was worried too, but she wanted to find the original notice before passing the message on.
sentences.zh: 佳也很担心，但她想先找到原始通知，再传播这条消息。

sentences.en: The article was two years old and described a different college with a similar name.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章是两年前的，讲的是另一所名字相似的学校。

sentences.en: When Jia checked her own library's website, she found only a plan to repair one reading room during the summer.
sentences.zh: 佳查看自己学校图书馆的网站后，只找到一项暑期维修一间阅览室的计划。

sentences.en: She posted the correct notice in the group and explained where the confusion had started.
sentences.zh: 她把正确通知发到群里，并解释误解从何而来。

sentences.en: The incident did not mean that every surprising story was false.
sentences.zh: 这件事并不意味着所有令人惊讶的消息都是假的。

sentences.en: It showed why dates, places, and original sources matter, especially when a headline makes us angry or afraid.
sentences.zh: 它说明日期、地点和原始来源为何重要，尤其是在标题引起愤怒或恐惧时。

sentences.en: A short pause before sharing can save many people from an unnecessary worry.
sentences.zh: 转发前稍作停顿，可能让许多人免去不必要的担忧。

sentences.en: Jia now asks who published a message and when, even if it comes from someone she trusts.
sentences.zh: 现在即使消息来自信任的人，佳也会问是谁发布的、何时发布的。

grammar.en: Jia was worried too, but she wanted to find the original notice before passing the message on.
grammar.zh: 佳也很担心，但她想先找到原始通知，再传播这条消息。
grammar.main: she wanted to find the original notice
grammar.subject: she
grammar.modifiers: before passing the message on 是介词加动名词结构，表示转发前。
grammar.logic: but 表示她虽然担忧，仍选择先核实。

grammar.en: It showed why dates, places, and original sources matter, especially when a headline makes us angry or afraid.
grammar.zh: 它说明日期、地点和原始来源为何重要，尤其是在标题引起愤怒或恐惧时。
grammar.main: It showed why sources matter
grammar.subject: It
grammar.modifiers: especially 引出强调；when 引导时间状语从句。
grammar.logic: why 从句解释核实信息的重要性，而非说明所有报道都不可信。

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the article?
options: To warn students against reading news
To announce a year-long library closure
To encourage checking information before sharing
To prove that libraries are disappearing
quiz.evidence: A short pause before sharing can save many people from an unnecessary worry.
quiz.explain: 全文围绕一次误传展开，落点是转发前核对来源、日期和地点。
whyWrong: 作者鼓励核实，不是拒绝新闻。
关闭一年的消息正是误传内容。
文中并未讨论图书馆整体消失。

quiz.question: What was actually planned at Jia's college?
options: The removal of all books
Repairs to one reading room
A complete closure for a year
A move to another city
quiz.evidence: When Jia checked her own library's website, she found only a plan to repair one reading room during the summer.
quiz.explain: 官方网站只有暑期修缮一间阅览室的计划。
whyWrong: 文中没有移走所有图书的安排。
整年关闭属于另一所学校的旧消息。
文中没有迁往另一城市。

quiz.question: Why can an emotional headline require extra care?
options: It may encourage people to react before checking
It always identifies the correct place
It proves that the story is false
It makes the publication date irrelevant
quiz.evidence: It showed why dates, places, and original sources matter, especially when a headline makes us angry or afraid.
quiz.explain: 同学们未打开链接便转发或抱怨，体现情绪可能催促未经核实的反应。
whyWrong: 相似校名恰恰导致地点误认。
作者没有把情绪性标题等同于假消息。
日期正是本次核实的重要依据。

title: Shade on the Walk Home

sentences.en: During a hot week, Rui noticed that one street felt more comfortable than the others on his walk home.
sentences.zh: 在炎热的一周里，瑞发现回家路上有一条街比其他街道更舒适。

sentences.en: It was lined with trees, whose branches shaded much of the pavement in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 街道两旁种着树，午后枝叶遮住了大部分人行道。

sentences.en: The next street had wider roads and newer buildings, but very little shade.
sentences.zh: 下一条街的道路更宽，建筑更新，却几乎没有树荫。

sentences.en: Rui's class decided to study the difference with their teacher instead of relying only on how the streets felt.
sentences.zh: 瑞的班级决定与老师一起研究这种差异，而非仅凭对街道的感受下结论。

sentences.en: They measured temperatures in shaded and sunny places at the same time on several afternoons.
sentences.zh: 他们在几个下午的同一时刻，测量阴凉处和日晒处的温度。

sentences.en: They also recorded traffic and wind, because these conditions could affect the results.
sentences.zh: 他们还记录交通和风的情况，因为这些条件可能影响结果。

sentences.en: Their small project could not explain every difference between the streets, yet it helped them ask better questions.
sentences.zh: 这个小项目不能解释街道间的所有差异，却帮助他们提出了更好的问题。

sentences.en: Where could new trees grow without blocking a crossing, and who would water them in dry weather?
sentences.zh: 哪些地方能在不挡住路口的情况下种树，干燥天气里又由谁浇水呢？

sentences.en: The students learned that making a cooler neighbourhood involves both good ideas and long-term care.
sentences.zh: 学生们明白了，让社区更凉爽既需要好主意，也需要长期养护。

sentences.en: They presented their notes to the school, including the questions that their measurements had not yet answered.
sentences.zh: 他们向学校展示了笔记，包括那些测量尚未解答的问题。

grammar.en: It was lined with trees, whose branches shaded much of the pavement in the afternoon.
grammar.zh: 街道两旁种着树，午后枝叶遮住了大部分人行道。
grammar.main: It was lined with trees
grammar.subject: It
grammar.modifiers: with trees 表示排列的事物；whose branches 引导非限制性定语从句。
grammar.logic: whose 表所属关系，把树与枝叶提供树荫联系起来。

grammar.en: They also recorded traffic and wind, because these conditions could affect the results.
grammar.zh: 他们还记录交通和风的情况，因为这些条件可能影响结果。
grammar.main: They also recorded traffic and wind
grammar.subject: They
grammar.modifiers: because 引导原因状语从句，解释记录其他条件的理由。
grammar.logic: 结果可能受多种条件影响，因此需要一并记录。

quiz.question: What does the class project help the students understand?
options: Trees need no attention after planting
A cooler neighbourhood needs investigation and continuing care
New buildings always lower street temperatures
Measuring once settles every question
quiz.evidence: The students learned that making a cooler neighbourhood involves both good ideas and long-term care.
quiz.explain: 调查后的问题涉及种在哪里和谁来浇水，末句强调想法与长期照料。
whyWrong: 谁负责浇水是文中明确提出的问题。
新建筑所在街道反而少有树荫。
学生多次测量，且承认项目有局限。

quiz.question: Why did the class record traffic and wind?
options: These conditions might influence the results
They wanted to design a new bus
Their teacher had lost a traffic map
They were counting sunny days
quiz.evidence: They also recorded traffic and wind, because these conditions could affect the results.
quiz.explain: because 从句直接说明这些条件可能影响结果。
whyWrong: 文中没有设计公交车的计划。
老师丢地图并非文章情节。
记录对象不仅是晴天数量。

quiz.question: How does the writer view the small project?
options: A final answer to every heat problem
A waste because it was small
A replacement for watering trees
Useful despite its limits
quiz.evidence: Their small project could not explain every difference between the streets, yet it helped them ask better questions.
quiz.explain: could not explain every difference 与 helped them ask better questions 表明其有限但有用。
whyWrong: 作者明确承认它不能解释所有差异。
项目帮助提出问题，并非浪费。
测量无法替代后续的实际养护。
